record.paper_title: Developments and open problems on chiral polytopes
record.original_question: Determine whether there are infinite families of chiral quotients of every regular honeycomb in hyperbolic 3-space, 4-space, and 5-space.

evidence.quote: Problem 23 Determine the existence of infinite families of chiral quotients of all regular honeycombs in hyperbolic 3-, 4- and 5-space.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An abstract polytope is a ranked partially ordered set satisfying the standard incidence axioms generalizing the face lattice of a convex polytope. Its automorphism group acts on flags (maximal chains). The polytope is called regular if this action is transitive on all flags; it is called chiral if the automorphism group has exactly two orbits on flags, with adjacent flags lying in different orbits (so the polytope has maximal rotational symmetry but admits no reflection-type automorphism). A regular honeycomb in hyperbolic n-space is a regular tessellation of hyperbolic n-space H^n by congruent regular polytopes filling space face-to-face; the regular honeycombs of H^3, H^4, and H^5 are the classical ones given by their Schläfli symbols (e.g., {3,5,3}, {4,3,5}, {5,3,4}, {5,3,5} in H^3; {3,3,3,5}, {5,3,3,3}, {5,3,3,4}, {4,3,3,5}, {5,3,3,5}, {3,4,3,4} in H^4; {3,3,3,4,3}, {3,4,3,3,3}, {3,4,3,3,4}, {4,3,3,4,3} in H^5).

A chiral quotient of a regular honeycomb H is a finite abstract polytope obtained as a quotient of H (equivalently, of its automorphism group acting on flags) that is itself chiral as an abstract polytope.

For each regular honeycomb H in hyperbolic 3-space, hyperbolic 4-space, and hyperbolic 5-space, determine whether there exists an infinite family of finite chiral abstract polytopes that arise as chiral quotients of H.

status_evidence.title: Chiral polytopes from hyperbolic honeycombs - Schulte, Weiss
status_evidence.snippet: Using modular quotients of linear groups over the Eisenstein ring Z[ω], infinite families of finite regular or chiral polytopes of types {3,3,6}, {3,6,3} and {6,3,6} are constructed.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress exists for some H^3 honeycombs, but no comprehensive resolution covering H^3, H^4, H^5 is recorded.

status_evidence.title: Chiral Polyhedra in 3-Dimensional Geometries and from a Petrie–Coxeter Construction
status_evidence.snippet: Extends to hyperbolic and projective spaces some structural results on chiral polyhedra.
status_evidence.claim: Active research continues on chiral polyhedra in hyperbolic geometry, with the higher-dimensional honeycomb question not reported as solved.
